description: Mixed attention effect (row 1). Two solid CRFs (attended slightly above unattended) close together, both sigmoidal; they overlap at low contrast, separate by ~0.03-0.05 across mid contrast, and re-converge at high contrast to a shared plateau near 0.94 (NOT 1.0). Dashed percent-modulation (right axis) is a BROAD, rounded interior bump peaking ~25% at mid-low contrast (x~0.05-0.06), rising gently from ~8% at the low-contrast foot and declining gently toward ~2% at high contrast.

provenance.figure_type: line/curve CRF, log-x, two same-colour solid sigmoids (left axis) plus one dashed bell (% modulation, right axis)
provenance.tool_rationale: Mode-1 quantitative plot. detect_plot_box located the axis rectangle as a hint; verified by longest-dark-run column/row profile. trace_darkest_in_band (per-column dark-cluster decomposition) separated the two solids by row band and isolated the dashed bump by its own lower region. resample_pchip for rounded apex / flat plateau. overlay for the single validation pass.

calibration.axis_lines_measured: left axis col 56.5 (NOT the label-text edge ~col 41), right axis col 189.5, plot top row 22, bottom row 201 — all read off the longest-consecutive-dark-run profile, not detect_plot_box density.

per_curve.attended: traced as the UPPER of the two solid dark clusters per column (darkness-weighted cluster centroid). Coincident with unattended at the shared foot (x<0.02, both y~0.235); a genuine ~0.03-0.05 attended-above gap opens through mid-contrast and re-converges near the plateau.
per_curve.unattended: traced as the LOWER solid cluster per column; same shared foot, lags attended through the rise.
per_curve.percent_modulation: dashed bell, traced as the LOWEST dark cluster per column AFTER explicitly separating it from the two solids' shared foot (the solids' foot sits at left-axis y~0.235, i.e. image rows ~155-159, which the prior pass mis-read as the bump's left flank). Per-column 3-cluster decomposition (two rising solids + one bell) gives the true dashed crest: foot ~8% (rows ~186) at x~0.011, rising gently through rows 182/176/169/162 to a BROAD rounded apex ~25% (rows 156-158) centered at x~0.052-0.06, then descending gently (rows 161/165/170/179/185) to ~8% at x~0.14 and tailing to ~2% (near the bottom axis) at x>0.3. Apex deliberately NOT over-sampled (single broad shoulder, two points x=0.052/0.060 at ~24.5-24.8%) so PCHIP renders a rounded broad top with no spike.

provenance.normalization: paper shared sub-1.0 scale; both solid plateaus ~0.94, NOT pinned to 1.0. Right axis % modulation 0-100 read independently.
provenance.bump_fix_note_2026-06-03: Reviewer flagged a 'weird bump' (sharp left-shifted spike) on the blue %-modulation curve in overlay_3C. Diagnosis (via crop_region zooms of the bump region on both paper and overlay, upscale 6-8x, plus a per-column 3-cluster darkness decomposition with the tick-anchored col-56.5 calibration): the dashed bump had been digitized with its apex too tall (29.5%) and too far left (x~0.029) and its low-contrast foot too low (7.9%), because the two solids' shared foot (left-axis y~0.235 -> rows ~155-159) was mistaken for the bump's left flank. The true paper bump is a BROAD rounded ~25% apex centered at x~0.052-0.06 with an ~8% foot. Only percent_modulation points + this provenance changed; the two solid CRFs were left untouched (verified identical). Re-rendered overlay_3C.png with the same tick-anchored left calibration (cols 56.5/189.5, rows 201/22) drawing %mod as value/100; adversarial crop_region re-check shows the blue crest now tracks the paper dashed ink to within 0.5% modulation worst-case (apex paper 24.9% vs render 24.7%), no PCHIP overshoot (rendered peak 24.7%).
provenance.calibration_note_vs_prior_audit: The 2026-06-03 audit's 'rising-flank-too-high / c50-too-low' finding traces to that audit using left axis col 41.5 (the tick-LABEL edge) instead of the true axis line col 56.5. That mislabels each pixel column with an x ~one notch too high, so audit paper-reads at 'x=0.073' were actually image columns near x=0.054. Re-checked with the correct col-56.5 calibration: the solid rising-flank values match the true pixel cluster centroids to within ~0.002 (e.g. x=0.0732 -> y 0.634 measured vs 0.635 prior). The solid CRFs were already faithful; this pass re-verifies them with recorded anchors and fixes only the dashed-bump kink/apex.
caveats: No numeric x ticks on the axis (only Log Contrast tick marks); x_range [0.01,1.0] (2 log decades) taken from the frame, consistent across panels 3A-3F.
The two solids share an identical foot and are only ~0.03-0.05 apart through the rise; their split is the genuine attended-above gap visible in the mid-contrast pixels, not an invented offset.

Dashed apex height/position carry ~+/-1.5% and ~+/-0.3 log-step uncertainty: the dash gaps and the rising lower-solid (whose foot rides through the bump's left region) make a few columns ambiguous; apex taken as x~0.052-0.06, ~25% (broad rounded top). The PRIOR pass placed the apex at x~0.03, ~29% by conflating the solids' foot with the bump's left flank — that left-shifted/over-tall apex plus dense apex sampling produced the PCHIP spike the reviewer flagged on overlay_3C; corrected here.
Right-axis % modulation calibration assumes the right tick frame shares the plot's top/bottom rows (no intermediate numeric ticks legible).
provenance.re_digitization_2026_06_04: X-AXIS RE-LABELED to the AUTHOR contrast window [1e-5, 1] (paper/code/attentionModel/Figure3C.m cRange=[1e-5 1]; CODE-013/014/015/018). The paper panel has NO numeric x ticks, so the prior pass guessed the left frame edge at 0.01 (2 decades); the authors' script axis floor is 1e-5. The CURVE INK on the paper is unchanged - this is a pure x-axis frame RELABEL: each traced point keeps its exact pixel position, its contrast value is recomputed from the SAME log-fractional position across the frame under the author window (c_new = lo*(hi/lo)^f, f = the point's fractional log-x position in the old frame). The calibration.x pixel-col anchors were relabeled likewise. The overlay_*.png (ink-on-paper) is therefore still pixel-faithful; only the x-axis tick labels move. Resolution authority: author code (Phase-A resolver ladder rung 1). This closes the PAPER_ISSUE digitized-window tripwire (test_audit_2026_06_04_supplement.py) and makes the half-max / left-shift claims testable in-window.
